title: Ensemble sensitivity sweep + decision memo (May 2024)
body:
Executive summary:

This note documents a focused bakeoff run we did in May 2024 to evaluate ensemble-style serving and prompt-sensitivity across three candidate model versions (rci-1.0, rci-1.1, and rci-ensemble-lite). The goal was to understand whether a small ensemble (majority vote + confidence tie-break) improves robustness on edge prompt cohorts without regressing core QoR, and to capture the cost/latency tradeoffs for Dedicated vs Hosted.

Key takeaways:
- rci-1.1 beats rci-1.0 on our held-out edge prompt shard (A/B score delta +5.6 absolute on human rateability) with negligible latency change (+6ms median).
- rci-ensemble-lite reduces critical failure cases (hallucinated facts; defined list) by ~42% vs rci-1.0 on an edge cohort, but increases median p50 latency by ~28ms and CPU/GPU token cost by ~1.9x in our Dedicated config.
- Small ensembles show asymmetric wins: they help in low-context, instruction-ambiguous prompts but can amplify repetitive-safe answers for conversational multi-turn prompts.
- We recommend rolling rci-1.1 to staged traffic (canary 10%) with an ensemble-fallback policy enabled only for high-risk routes (classification/qa-critical) where latency budget allows.

Methodology (high level):
- Datasets: held-out prompt shards from production telemetry (edge_shard_v2, 3.1k prompts), curated stress prompts (fact-check, numeric reasoning, instruction-ambiguity, 1.8k prompts), and standard devset (50k examples) used for regression detection.
- Promptset variants: baseline prompts, adversarial rephrases (4 rephrases per prompt), and truncated-prefix versions to simulate low-context.
- Models tested: rci-1.0 (deployed baseline), rci-1.1 (small architecture + tiny instruction-tuning update), rci-ensemble-lite (rci-1.0 + rci-1.1 + rci-0.9 distilled, simple majority + confidence heuristics).
- Metrics: automated metrics (BLEU-like for structured outputs, token-level F1 for extraction tasks), human rateability (3-judge majority on helpfulness/accuracy), safety flags, regression delta on primary intents, and real cost (tokens * billing rate + infra multiplier).
- Infrastructure config: Hosted API default concurrency; Dedicated test pool with 4x A100 equivalent. Batching kept identical across models for fairness.

Leaderboard (top-level aggregated scores, normalized 0-100 where higher is better):
- rci-1.1: 82.3
- rci-ensemble-lite: 80.1
- rci-1.0: 76.7

Win/loss snapshot (edge_shard_v2, human majority rateability):
- rci-1.1 vs rci-1.0: wins 1,142 | losses 486 | ties 40  (win rate +9.2% absolute)
- ensemble-lite vs rci-1.1: wins 332 | losses 229 | ties 17  (small net improvement on edge shard)

Per-cohort notes:
- Fact-check cohort: ensemble-lite reduces hallucination false-positive rate from 18.6% -> 10.8% vs rci-1.0. rci-1.1 reduces it to 12.1%.
- Numeric-reasoning: rci-1.1 shows a small but consistent improvement in exact-match (EM +3.8 pts) vs rci-1.0. ensemble-lite helps only on truncated prompts where single-model outputs diverge.
- Instruction-ambiguity: ensemble-lite sometimes selects conservative answers (safer but less helpful). We measured a 7% drop in helpfulness score in this cohort relative to rci-1.1.

Statistical testing and significance:
- Paired bootstrap for human labels; rci-1.1 vs rci-1.0 differences significant at p<0.01 for the edge_shard_v2 and fact-check cohorts. ensemble-lite gains on hallucination reduction are significant p<0.05 but come with increased latency variance.

Cost and latency tradeoffs (observed):
- p50 latency (Hosted default): rci-1.0 128ms | rci-1.1 134ms | ensemble-lite 162ms
- p95 latency: rci-1.0 412ms | rci-1.1 428ms | ensemble-lite 612ms
- Relative per-token cost (Dedicated test profile): rci-1.0 1.0x | rci-1.1 1.02x | ensemble-lite 1.9x
- Tail latency and cost variability with ensemble-lite grows under higher concurrency; in Dedicated we saw queuing increases past 75% utilization.

Qualitative failure modes observed:
- Ensemble amplification: when two models produce near-identical but wrong answers, majority vote solidifies the wrong output (observed on domain-specific jargon).
- Over-conservatism: ensemble tended to produce generic safe responses for ambiguous instructions which reduced helpfulness metrics.
- Prompt-sensitivity: rephrase experiments show rci-1.1 is less sensitive than rci-1.0 (measured by variance in scores across 4 rephrasings), and ensemble-lite reduces variance further for fact-check prompts.

Decision rationale and recommendation:
- Primary rollout: promote rci-1.1 to hosted default (staged canary 10% -> 50% over 7 days) because it improves QoR across key cohorts with minimal latency/cost changes. This aligns with product desire to improve quality without shaving latency SLAs.
- Ensemble usage: do not enable ensemble-lite globally. Instead, implement a policy to enable ensemble-lite only for routes flagged as high-risk/low-volume (e.g., legal-qa, financial-qa, customer-critical classification) where the latency budget can be extended and extra cost is justified. Put ensemble behind a feature flag and a per-route config in the routing layer.
- Monitoring & rollback criteria: regression >1.5 pts absolute on core devset intent accuracy OR p95 latency increase >20% for a route should immediately halt rollout. Also add a weekly human-sampling audit for ensemble routes for first month.

Operational notes / Implementation checklist:
- Product: add per-route ensemble flag UI in Console and document recommended use-cases. (Owners: Priya Nair, Product Console)
- Infra: add autoscaling headroom recommendation for Dedicated when ensemble routes exceed 5% of traffic. (Owner: Diego Alvarez)
- Applied ML: ship rci-1.1 model artifact to model-catalog with quantization profile; add ensemble-lite serving blueprint to Infra repo for smoke tests. (Owner: Maya Chen)
- QA: run a 1k human sample on canary traffic after 24h and 7 days; compare to baseline. (Owner: Noah Brooks)

Open questions and risks:
- Long-term cost model: if ensemble adoption expands, Dedicated cost multiples become material; need forecast scenarios for TCO.
- Edge distribution drift: we saw 2.3% of prompts in edge_shard_v2 that are newly emergent; need ongoing shard refresh cadence (recommended monthly).
- Failure taxonomy: more granular labeling required to understand when ensemble amplifies vs mitigates errors.

Appendix (quick links and artifacts):
- Raw leaderboard CSV: gs://redwood-evals/ensemble_sweep/may2024/leaderboard.csv
- Human eval rubric: internal doc link (see PR #412)
- Jupyter notebooks: https://github.com/redwood-inference/curation/tree/main/evals/ensemble_sweep

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally conservative: recommendation biases toward small model change (rci-1.1) for broad rollout and limited, controlled ensemble use. Please review the rollout guard thresholds and suggest any route exceptions.
- If product wants blanket safety increases for all QA routes, we should run a second cost-sensitivity study focused on autoscale economics (I can scope that).

Draft history:
- 2024-05-08 initial run and draft
- 2024-05-15 added human eval tranche, updated stats
- 2024-05-22 internal review edits and decision language

-- End of memo --
